_comment: Written by the agent each day (3 EN post ideas for the operator). Keep facts and numbers traceable to posts on the board. Short hyphen only, no new numbers.

ideas.title: Fancy agent memory still loses to boring RAG
ideas.hook_en: A new Memory Tax paper tested 11 agent memory systems on LongMemEval-s. None of them beat plain RAG over the raw chat history. Chunk, hybrid search, rerank. That is it. As someone who spends days on Milvus and Ops Agent memory, this hurts in a good way. Stop shipping a clever store before your boring retrieval baseline is honest.
ideas.video_tip: 20s talking-head: whiteboard with 11 fancy memory logos crossed out, one box left labeled 'chunk + hybrid + rerank' with a green check; flash the LongMemEval-s line as caption.
ideas.angle: yin min Milvus / Memory ambassador reaction to Memory Tax result — first-principles retrieval before fancy agent memory.
ideas.why: Outsider @manthanguptaa Memory Tax post 7.6K views; Claude Code context-reload debate on @dotey 28.9K; Memory/RAG + AI Agent keywords strong among >=5k hits.

ideas.title: Unlimited AI tokens is not an architecture
ideas.hook_en: Cisco's president gave a 27-year-old unlimited AI access to rewrite 98 percent of legacy code in two years. The Chinese timeline of that story already crossed 78K views. I lead an ops team and I build with Codex every day, so this hits close. Unlimited tokens are cheap courage. What I still want on the board is the blast radius, the rollback, and who owns the night the rewrite fails.
ideas.video_tip: 25s talking-head: slide 'unlimited AI' big and green, then stamp three red ops chips over it — blast radius / rollback / on-call owner — while the Cisco 98% line stays as subtitle.
ideas.angle: yin min DevOps / Ops Agent lens on the Cisco unlimited-AI rewrite story — tokens vs judgment and ownership.
ideas.why: @dotey Cisco/Paddy rewrite post 78.2K views; coding-agent chatter also includes @0xlangeai WorkBuddy vs Codex 35.5K.

ideas.title: Thousands of agents as your red team
ideas.hook_en: Anthropic just set thousands of Claude agents loose to hunt subtle emergent misalignment — automated red-teaming because humans run out of hours. That research post is already past 350K views. I keep thinking about my Ops Agent the same way. One clever prompt is a demo. A fleet that keeps poking the same failure mode overnight is an ops practice.
ideas.video_tip: 20s screencast: spawn a terminal grid of many agent workers labeled 'probe / evade / report', then collapse them into one overnight red-team job queue next to an Ops Agent logo.
ideas.angle: yin min Ops Agent builder reading Anthropic's multi-agent red-team research as a pattern for continuous ops probing.
ideas.why: @AnthropicAI automated misalignment research 350.5K views; self-assessment still at 1.96M as background safety meta; Claude/Agent keywords led the lexicon counts.
